tagline: South from Dayville, past a town named for a brand.
intro: At Dayville, where the South Fork meets the John Day, South Fork Road turns south off US 26 and follows the smaller river up its canyon for 50 miles of gravel to the Malheur National Forest. The walls are Columbia River basalt. Stands of old-growth ponderosa pine grow along the way with Douglas fir and white fir, and willows line the road.
Somewhere along the way the river drops 56 feet over Izee Falls. The Rockpile Ranch, started in the late 1800s, is still working beside the road.

moments.title: Black Canyon East Trailhead
moments.text: Nine miles south of Dayville a trailhead leaves the road for the Black Canyon Wilderness, in the drainage of the same river.

moments.title: Izee
moments.text: A ranching community named for a rancher's I.Z. cattle brand, where the two-room schoolhouse took its last pupils in 1989 and now hosts community gatherings.

practical: The road is high-standard gravel suited to most passenger cars, but some stretches are only one vehicle wide, and there is no cell service along it.
